review_context: Second runnable L&E replay family slice adding wage/hour clean synthetic actuals and carrier rejection inputs.
finding_title: Multi-family replay input packs need family binding in addition to case-ID binding.
finding_summary: When a second L&E family becomes runnable, same-case budget and preflight IDs are not enough. A schema-valid discrimination budget can be declared under a wage/hour replay slot unless the input-pack validator compares the payload matter family with the builder-binding family.
observable_context: The replay input-pack manifest now includes direct runnable wage/hour clean inputs for actuals variance and carrier rejection capture.
The existing validator already checked local path containment, schema validity, no-write flags, and same-case budget/preflight anchors for generated reports.
The second-family scout identified that manifest entries are keyed by learning fixture and loop type, while payloads still need to match the binding case family.
The implemented guard rejects a legal_budget_proposal.json whose matter_family does not match the L&E builder-binding family for the replay slot.
observable_decision_logic: A replay input can be schema-valid and internally coherent while still representing the wrong legal family.
Wrong-family budget anchors are especially risky because downstream actuals and carrier bundles can inherit or bind to the wrong budget identity.
The first stable guard should remain Python/Pydantic because the semantics are still evolving and are authority-sensitive.
Rust remains a future leaf-tool candidate for path, schema, flag, and identity scans after Python tests define the exact oracle behavior.
solution_path: Add wage/hour clean synthetic replay budget, actuals, and carrier rejection source bundle under examples/synthetic/labor-employment/replay-inputs/wage-hour-clean.
Extend the L&E replay input-pack manifest with wage/hour actuals and carrier-capture entries.
Pass binding-case family into the input validator and compare legal budget proposal matter_family to that expected family.
Add direct wage/hour builder tests for actuals variance and carrier rejection capture.
Add a wrong-family budget-anchor regression test that points wage/hour slots at the discrimination budget and expects the audit to block.
applies_when: A replay input-pack manifest declares inputs for more than one L&E fixture family.
A local budget proposal artifact has a matter_family field and is used as an anchor for a replay slot.
A future bulk checker needs to distinguish same-case identity from same-family fixture validity.
does_not_apply_when: A report is intentionally cross-family aggregate evidence with an explicit aggregate contract.
The artifact lacks a family-bearing field and must be checked by a stronger downstream contract instead.
The issue concerns production matter matching under an Orchestrator-owned runtime contract.
danger_if_misapplied: If a second runnable family can use a first-family budget anchor, QA may report broader synthetic coverage while actually replaying the wrong legal budget assumptions.
suggested_actions: DAD should classify wrong-family replay inputs separately from wrong-case ID mismatches.
DAD should track which artifacts carry family identity and which require downstream aggregate binding checks.
Do not port this to Rust until Python tests cover family, variant, executable fixture, and outcome seed binding semantics.
reviewer_notes: This record contains synthetic fixture references only.
It records observable evidence, decision logic, fix refs, and test refs without hidden chain-of-thought.
red_team_notes: Do not treat more runnable families as better coverage unless their payloads are family-bound.
Do not let local family names become canonical Semantic Substrate taxonomy from the intake repo.
Do not add Rust for this semantic check until the contract stabilizes.
